name: Cooking Video Ideas
blurb: 45 cooking and food content ideas with a 2-second hook and format for each
title: 45 Cooking Video Ideas and Food Content Ideas (With Hooks)
description: 45 cooking video ideas for Shorts, TikTok and Reels: quick recipes, kitchen skills, food stories and sketches, each with what to film, a hook and a format.
h1: 45 Cooking Video Ideas, Each With a Hook and Format
answer: This list is for home cooks and food creators who want ideas they can film in an ordinary kitchen with one phone. Each idea says what to cook or show, the hook for the first two seconds and the format that suits it.

items.d: Make a full meal from three basics, like eggs, rice and greens. Hook: the three items lined up on the counter. Format: hands only, overhead.
Cook everything in a single pan with a timer on screen. Hook: the timer starting as the egg cracks. Format: overhead timelapse.
Turn one bowl of cold rice into fried rice, a rice cake and soup. Hook: the sad cold bowl. Format: hands only.
Make a chilled dessert with a fridge and a bowl. Hook: the spoon cracking the finished top. Format: hands only.

items.t: A lunchbox for the whole week
items.d: Batch-cook and pack five boxes. Hook: five filled boxes stacked. Format: timelapse.

items.t: Dinner from what is left in the fridge
items.d: Open the fridge, pick what is there and improvise. Hook: the nearly empty shelf. Format: POV.
Recreate a dish you love from a market stall, in your own style. Hook: the first bite with a crunch. Format: hands and voice-over.

items.t: A sauce you can make in one minute
items.d: Mix a sauce and show three dishes it goes on. Hook: the pour. Format: close-up.
Cook a quick dish in a mug using a microwave. Hook: the mug coming out steaming. Format: hands only.

items.t: Cut an onion without the mess
items.d: Show a clean slicing method step by step. Hook: perfect even slices falling apart. Format: close-up, hands only.

items.t: How to tell when oil is ready
items.d: Show the visual signs with a wooden chopstick test. Hook: bubbles forming around the chopstick. Format: close-up.
Show five folds side by side. Hook: the prettiest fold first. Format: overhead.
Demonstrate a safe grip and the claw hand. Hook: a slow-motion slice. Format: hands only.

items.t: Rescue a dish that is too salty
items.d: Show simple fixes like adding more base or acid. Hook: the grimace after tasting. Format: talking head plus close-ups.

items.t: Cook rice without a rice cooker
items.d: Pot method with a lid and timing on screen. Hook: lifting the lid on fluffy rice. Format: overhead.
Show the jar method and the paper towel method. Hook: wilted herbs next to fresh ones. Format: comparison.
Teach the move slowly, then at speed. Hook: the clean crack. Format: close-up.
Simple method with water and baking soda. Hook: the burnt bottom shown close up. Format: before and after.

items.t: A dish my family always cooks
items.d: Cook it while telling one memory attached to it. Hook: the dish on the table. Format: voice-over.
Follow a handwritten recipe card, with their permission. Hook: the card held up. Format: hands and voice-over.
Try a new dish and give a fair score. Hook: the final plate and the score. Format: talking head.

items.t: A food rule from my home country
items.d: Explain one table custom or habit. Hook: the rule in big text. Format: talking head.

items.t: The meal that taught me to cook
items.d: Tell how you learned while cooking it again. Hook: the first sizzle. Format: voice-over.

items.t: Older relative reviews a trendy snack
items.d: A grandparent tastes a new snack and gives their verdict. Hook: their face on first bite. Format: talking head.

items.t: What I cook when I am tired
items.d: Your laziest real meal. Hook: you dropping your bag by the door. Format: POV.

items.t: Food I hated as a kid, cooked now
items.d: Give a childhood enemy a second chance. Hook: the ingredient held at arm's length. Format: talking head.
Learn a dish from a friend or neighbour who agreed to appear. Hook: their hands showing a trick. Format: interview.
A polite standoff over the last piece of pizza, where everyone insists the others have it. Hook: three hands hovering over the box. Format: 3-person sketch.

items.t: The delivery that went to the wrong door
items.d: Neighbours discover they ordered the same dish. Hook: the bag with the wrong name. Format: sketch.
A classroom lunch mystery where the self-appointed detective is not what he seems. Hook: the empty lunch bag held upside down. Format: sketch.
Everyone tries to bring up big news at the same dinner. Hook: three people saying I have an announcement. Format: sketch.
A couple knocks the last cookie to the floor and one invents new rules to claim it. Hook: the cookie falling in slow motion. Format: 2-person sketch.

items.t: A cooking show that goes wrong
items.d: Play a confident TV chef whose every step fails. Hook: Today we make the perfect pancake. Format: sketch.
Caption what the recipe says next to what happens. Hook: the first instruction on screen. Format: split screen.

items.t: The kitchen timer that judges you
items.d: Give the timer a voice that comments on your cooking. Hook: the first beep and a sigh. Format: voice-over sketch.

items.t: Explaining a dish to a foreign friend
items.d: Describe a local dish while a friend guesses what it is. Hook: the covered plate. Format: sketch.

items.t: Cook every dish from one region
items.d: A weekly series working through one cuisine. Hook: the map or list with the first one ticked. Format: series.
Set your own spending limit and show the receipt. Hook: the receipt total first. Format: vlog.
Cook one ingredient a new way each day. Hook: the ingredient and day count. Format: series.

items.t: Guess the dish from the sound
items.d: Play cooking sounds before the reveal. Hook: a sizzle on a black screen. Format: no-face.

items.t: Remake a dish from a photo only
items.d: Try to copy a dish without a recipe. Hook: the photo and your result split. Format: comparison.
Make a simple no-knife dish using only your other hand, carefully. Hook: the awkward first stir. Format: challenge.
Let comments pick three items for next time. Hook: the three picks on screen. Format: series.
Plate the same food as home style, cafe style and fancy. Hook: the fanciest plate first. Format: comparison.
Make a breakfast from a different country each week. Hook: the finished tray. Format: series.

sections.h: How to pick and film a cooking video
body: Pick a dish you already cook well for your first videos, so you can focus on filming instead of the recipe. Prep everything before you press record; cooking content is easier to cut when each step is a clean shot.

ol: Choose one idea and decide the money shot: the pour, the crack, the first bite.
Set the phone overhead or at a low angle beside the counter, with a window or lamp in front of the food.
Film each step as its own short clip and keep hands and the board tidy.
Cut to 15 to 60 seconds, put quantities in captions, and keep natural cooking sounds.
Post on a regular rhythm and turn ideas that work into series.

body.note: Keep knives, hot oil and open flames safe on camera. Do not suggest food as a cure for anything.

ul: Open on the money shot: the cut, the pour, the cheese pull.
Show the finished plate first, then rewind to the raw ingredients.
Start with a sound: the sizzle, the crunch, the crack.
Line up the only ingredients you will use.
State the constraint: One pan. Five minutes.
Begin with a mistake or a problem, like a burnt pan, and fix it.
Use a face reaction on the first bite.

faq.q: Do I need a nice kitchen to film cooking videos?
faq.a: No. Clear a small part of the counter, use one clean board and good light. Tight close-ups hide the rest of the kitchen.

faq.q: Can I film the food sketches for my channel?
faq.a: Yes. The Last Slice, Wrong Order Delivery and the other linked scripts are original and free under CC BY 4.0, including on monetised channels. Credit Script: cv.cm.

faq.q: Should I talk or just show the food?
faq.a: Both work. Hands-only videos with captions travel well across languages; voice-over adds personality. Try both and keep the one that feels natural.
